blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the chart of accounts is a strategic choice, not a technical one. Its structure decides which questions can be answered quickly from the books and which will take a week of reconstruction. A company that cannot see its profitability by customer segment without a special project has a chart of accounts that is quietly costing it decisions every month.

Good chart design starts from the decisions that leaders need to make. Which products are really profitable? Which customer groups are growing? Which costs are genuinely variable? Each of these questions implies a dimension in the chart — and designing with those dimensions in mind is far cheaper than retrofitting them once the business has grown.

For that reason, every senior finance leader should review the chart at least every two years — not for tidiness, but for decision readiness. It is a piece of infrastructure no board ever asks about, and one that quietly shapes every analytical conversation that follows.

items.q: According to the text, the chart of accounts is primarily…
items.why: "the chart of accounts is a strategic choice, not a technical one."

items.q: Where should good chart design begin?
options: from the software the company already owns
from the decisions leaders need to make
items.why: "Good chart design starts from the decisions that leaders need to make."

items.q: What does the author say about building dimensions into the chart early?
options: It is only worthwhile for large companies
It should be avoided until the business has grown
It is far cheaper than retrofitting them later
items.why: "designing with those dimensions in mind is far cheaper than retrofitting them once the business has grown."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Dimensions are cheaper to build in than to add afterwards.
The chart of accounts shapes which questions can be answered quickly.
The chart of accounts is a purely clerical matter that leaders can ignore.
A poorly designed chart imposes a hidden, recurring cost.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que o plano de contas é estratégico e molda decisões — não algo meramente burocrático.

items.q: By saying the chart is "infrastructure no board ever asks about," the author suggests that…
options: only the board can authorise changes to it
its influence is significant even though it goes unnoticed
it has no real effect on strategy
boards should approve the chart line by line
items.why: Inferência: infraestrutura invisível que "quietly shapes every analytical conversation" — importa muito, embora ninguém repare.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o redesenho do plano de contas à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time. Before I show you a single account, I want to be clear about the problem we're actually solving. Right now, when the board asks which customer segments are profitable, we can't answer without pulling three people off their work for a month. That's not a reporting gap — that's a design flaw.

The current chart was built to satisfy the auditors and nothing else. It's tidy, it reconciles, and it tells us almost nothing about where the money is really made. So what I'm proposing is that we rebuild it around a handful of dimensions the leadership actually asks about: segment, product line, and whether a cost is genuinely variable.

I would recommend that we agree those dimensions before we touch a single account number. If we get the questions right first, the structure almost designs itself. If we don't, we'll be retrofitting for years.

And one last thing — whatever we land on, let's commit to reviewing it every two years. Not to keep it neat, but to make sure it still answers the decisions we're facing then, which won't be the ones we're facing today.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What problem does Harry say the redesign is actually solving?
options: The chart fails to reconcile at month-end
The company cannot see which customer segments are profitable without a month of work
The auditors have rejected the current chart
items.why: "when the board asks which customer segments are profitable, we can't answer without pulling three people off their work for a month."

items.q: According to Harry, what was the current chart built to do?
options: Satisfy the auditors and little else
items.why: "The current chart was built to satisfy the auditors and nothing else."

items.q: What does Harry want the leadership to agree on before touching any account number?
options: The headcount for the finance team
The dimensions leaders actually ask about
items.why: "I would recommend that we agree those dimensions before we touch a single account number."

items.q: What does Harry imply by "the structure almost designs itself"?
options: The redesign can be automated by software
The old structure can simply be reused
No human judgement is needed at all
Once the right questions are settled, the structure follows naturally from them
items.why: Inferência: acertar as perguntas primeiro torna o desenho quase óbvio — o esforço está em definir as dimensões, não em desenhar contas.

items.q: Why does Harry want a review every two years?
options: To ensure it still answers the decisions the company will face then
To keep the chart neat and tidy
To reduce the number of accounts over time
Because auditors require a biennial review
items.why: "Not to keep it neat, but to make sure it still answers the decisions we're facing then, which won't be the ones we're facing today."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Answering that question today takes a full week of reconstruction." Here, reconstruction means…
options: painstakingly reassembling data the chart doesn't capture directly
items.why: Reconstruction = reconstrução: remontar manualmente dados que o plano de contas não entrega prontos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We simply cannot see our ___ by customer segment without a special project."
items.why: Profitability = lucratividade — o que a empresa não consegue enxergar por segmento.

items.q: "Each of those questions implies a dimension in the chart." A dimension here is…
options: the physical size of the ledger
the level of detail in a footnote
an axis along which results can be sliced and analysed
items.why: Dimension = dimensão: um eixo (segmento, produto, tipo de custo) pelo qual se corta a análise.

items.q: "Adding segment reporting now avoids having to retrofit it later." To retrofit means to…
options: design something correctly from the start
add a capability after the fact, usually at greater cost
outsource a process to a vendor
items.why: To retrofit = adaptar tarde: acrescentar depois algo que deveria ter sido previsto — quase sempre mais caro.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Review the chart for ___, not tidiness — can it still answer the decisions leaders face?"
items.why: Decision readiness = prontidão para decisão: o critério real da revisão, não a mera arrumação.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new chart of accounts." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new dimensions one entity at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, etapa por etapa.

items.q: "Two controllers pushed back on the extra segment coding." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the redesign but never followed through on the segment mapping." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Renumbering the accounts alone won't move the needle on decision speed." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
